spots.name: West Lake
spots.summary: West Lake, also known as Xihu and by other names, is a freshwater lake in Hangzhou, China. Situated to the west of Hangzhou's former walled city, the lake has a surface area of 6.39 km2 (2.47 sq mi), stretching 3.2 km (2.0 mi) from north to south and 2.8 km (1.7 mi) from east to west.

spots.name: Lingyin Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lingyin Temple is a prominent Chan Buddhist temple near Hangzhou that is renowned for its many pagodas and grottos. Its name is commonly and literally translated into English as Temple of the Soul's Retreat.

spots.name: Leifeng Pagoda
spots.summary: The Leifeng Pagoda is a five-story, eight-sided tower located on Sunset Hill south of West Lake in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. Originally constructed in the year AD 975, it collapsed in 1924 but was rebuilt in 2002. Since then, it has become a popular tourist attraction.

spots.name: Hangzhou Olympic Expo Center
spots.summary: The Hangzhou Olympic Expo Center or Hangzhou Olympic Sports Center is a multi-purpose sports complex in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China.

spots.name: Qiantang River Bridge
spots.summary: The Qiantang River Bridge is a combined road and railway bridge across the Qiantang River at Hangzhou in Zhejiang Province, China.

spots.name: Yue Fei Temple
spots.summary: The Yue Fei Temple, also known as Yuewang or King Yue Temple, is a traditional Chinese temple built around the tomb of the Song-era general Yue Fei in Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang Province in eastern China.

spots.name: Liuhe Pagoda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Liuhe Pagoda, literally Six Harmonies Pagoda, is a multi-story Chinese pagoda in southern Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, China. It is located at the foot of Yuelun Hill, facing the Qiantang River.

spots.name: Zhejiang Provincial Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Zhejiang Provincial Museum, also known as Zhejiang Memorial Museum of Revolutionary History, is the provincial museum of Zhejiang, China, located in Hangzhou. It was established in 1929 as the West Lake Museum on the Gushan Island in the West Lake. It houses over 100,000 items in its permanent collection.

spots.name: Xiling Seal Engravers' Society
spots.summary: The Xiling Seal Engravers' Society is a Chinese arts organisation based in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, PRC. It was founded in 1904 but, with antecedents dating back to the Ming and Qing dynasties, is one of China's most important traditional stone seal engraving associations.

spots.name: West Lake Cultural Square
spots.summary: West Lake Cultural Square is a square in the Xiacheng District of Hangzhou, China. It was built in 2002 and it covers an area of 36,000 m. It is used for science and performing arts exhibitions, entertainment, leisure, and also has a business centre. The ninth tallest building in Hangzhou is located at the square.

spots.name: Baochu Pagoda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Baochu Pagoda is a pagoda in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, China. Known as one of the landmarks of the West Lake, it is located just north of the lake on top of Precious Stone Hill. Its small base supports seven stories and gives it a distinctively slender and elegant appearance.

spots.name: Phoenix Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Phoenix Mosque is a mosque in Hangzhou, in the Zhejiang province of China. It is known for being one of the four great mosques of China. It is also one of the earliest mosque built in China. The origin of the mosque dates from the Tang or Song dynasty.

spots.name: Gongchen Bridge
spots.summary: The Gongchen Bridge is a historic stone arch bridge over the Grand Canal in Gongshu District of Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China.

spots.name: Hu Qing Yu Tang

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hu Qing Yu Tang was an important center of traditional Chinese medicine in the late 19th and early 20th century. Its site at 95 Dajing Lane (大井巷95号) in central Hangzhou, China, is now a TCM museum and drugstore with a prestigious reputation at the same level as the Tongrentang in Beijing.

spots.name: Broken Bridge
spots.summary: Broken Bridge is a bridge near the West Lake in Hangzhou, China. It is a small, three-span, semicircular stone arch. The current bridge was built in 1922 but its history dates from the Tang dynasty. It was known as Baoyou Bridge (寶祐橋) during the Song dynasty and Duanjia Bridge (段家橋) during the Yuan dynasty.

spots.summary: The Temple of the Qian Kings, also known by its Chinese name as the Qianwang or Qian Wang Temple, is a Chinese temple in Hangzhou, China, honoring the Qian family who ruled as kings of Wuyue in the 10th-century interregnum between the Tang and Song dynasties.

spots.name: Tomb of Yue Fei
spots.summary: The Tomb of Yue Fei, also known by its Chinese names Yue Fen and Yue Fei Mu, is the traditional Chinese tomb of the Song-era general Yue Fei located at his temple south of Qixia Hill (栖霞岭) and northwest of West Lake in Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang Province in eastern China.

spots.summary: Wulin Square is a square in the Xiacheng District of Hangzhou. It is served by the Wulin Square Station of the Hangzhou Metro.

spots.summary: The Hangzhou Civic Center or Citizen Center is a civic center in Jianggan District in central Hangzhou, the capital of China's Zhejiang province. It is located beside the Citizen Center Station on the Hangzhou Metro's Lines 4 and 7.

spots.name: Zhejiang Library
spots.summary: Zhejiang Library, sometimes abbreviated as Zhetu (浙图), is a public library in Hangzhou, China. Founded in 1900 during the Qing dynasty, it is among the earliest provincial public libraries in China.

spots.name: Korean Provisional Government Hangzhou Historic Site Memorial Hall
spots.summary: The Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea Memorial Hall is a museum and former temporary headquarters of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea located in Hangzhou, China. It was used by that government from May 1932 to November 1935.

spots.summary: Due to limitations on visitor numbers, visitors are encouraged to make a booking on WeChat before visiting the museum. However, this might not be practical to do if you can't read Chinese, as the booking system is in Chinese only. The museum has another branch in Anji.

spots.name: Evening Bell Ringing on Nanping Hill
spots.summary: A powerful bell in a temple on a mountain, rung at dusk. One does not need to visit the bell, it can be heard across the lake.

spots.name: Three Ponds Mirroring the Moon
spots.summary: Built in the early 1600s, this is the largest island on the lake. When there is a full moon, candles inside the pagodas are lit, and in the candle light it appears as though you see the moonlight (if you are romantic enough to see it), hence the name.

spots.name: Hubin Parks
spots.summary: Hubin Parks 1, 3, 6, and probably the numbers in between, are the parks between Hubin Road and the West Lake. Relatively newly designed as the West Lake Tunnel that goes underneath was being built in early 2004, these parks are good to sit for a bit, buy ice cream or a newspaper, and most importantly hire a boat from the cluster of boat docks at each park.

spots.name: Leifeng Pagoda in Evening Glow
spots.summary: The pagoda (see below for full description) is lit up at night. It is best viewed from across the lake, for example from the spot indicated here.

spots.name: Wushan Square
spots.summary: Wushan Square and Wushan Hill are major town centres in Hangzhou. The view from the top is excellent on a clear day, and there are also trails around the hills from behind the pagoda. The pagoda itself has been modernized with an elevator and nice open-air tea house at the top, but the original bell is still intact and in use.
